## Phase 1: Measure SimulationManager Internals

Add focused timing inside `SimulationManager.OnSystemTurn` / its private `OnNextTurn` loop.

Target stock anchor:

- `decompiled\Game.Session.Sim\SimulationManager.cs`

What to measure:

- Each `_turnUpdates` submanager name.
- Elapsed ms per submanager.
- Current day, turn, player id, and total players.
- Only log entries above a low threshold, around `4-6 ms`, to avoid excessive noise.

Pass criteria:

- The log identifies which simulation submanager causes the `24-49 ms` slice.
- Do not optimize yet unless the culprit is obvious and very low risk.

## Phase 2: Split SimulationManager Internally

If Phase 1 shows multiple simulation submanagers or one large repeated chunk, split the simulation submanager loop across frames.

Rules:

- Preserve vanilla `_turnUpdates` order.
- Do not enqueue human/other/system turn-start events until all pending simulation work is finished.
- Keep a pending-work state tied to the current `SessionContext`, day, and turn.
- Abort/fallback cleanly if context changes unexpectedly.

Pass criteria:

- No single `SimulationManager` system-turn slice regularly exceeds `12-16 ms`.
- Human turn resumes correctly after all simulation submanagers complete.
- No skipped submanager, duplicate submanager, or turn-order break appears in logs.

## Phase 2.7: After Prohibition Suite Ownership Audit

Goal: separate runtime ownership cleanly across the After Prohibition DLLs so `GameplayTweaks` stops doing mutation work that belongs in a feature DLL, while keeping `GameplayTweaks` as the turn pacing and compatibility coordinator.

This phase is about duplicate hot-path ownership, not file layout. Separate `.cs` files do not cause runtime lookup lag by themselves. Duplicate Harmony patches, duplicate scans, and duplicate mutation passes can.

Detailed audit doc:

- `docs\after-prohibition-suite-ownership-audit.md`

Current intended DLL ownership:

| DLL | Intended owner scope | Hot-path risk to audit |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AfterProhibitionAssets.dll` | asset registration and image replacement | startup/menu asset patching only; should not run turn-end scans |
| `AfterProhibitionCompatibility.dll` | external mod detection and protection matrix | should detect and expose ownership, not run repeated gameplay mutation |
| `AfterProhibitionEconomy.dll` | stock refresh, business module repair, economy classifiers and bridges | `BusinessUpdate.UpdateBusinessModules`, Dirty Cash sweeps, player legal consumers |
| `AfterProhibitionFamily.dll` | family, pregnancy, residential/family lifecycle | `PeopleTracker`, `PlayerInfo.OnPlayerTurnStarted`, residence/family turn work |
| `AfterProhibitionPolitics.dll` | politics setup and politics behavior ownership | `PoliticsManager.OnSystemTurn`, setup/tutorial starter hooks |
| `AfterProhibitionRoutes.dll` | vehicle route decisions, route shop orders, node authority | `CommandGoto`, route input, vehicle node checks |
| `AfterProhibitionUI.dll` | UI retheme, Crew HUD, aggro UI, portrait/crew visual guards | HUD refresh, crew pick refresh, popup/input hooks |
| `GameplayTweaks.dll` | turn pacing, performance slicing, compatibility shims, fallback guards | should avoid feature mutation when a suite DLL owns it |

## Phase 2.6C: Remove Reflection From Business Module Slicer

Status: implemented in `GameplayTweaks` and built in Release.

Evidence:

- Current live logs showed Phase 2.7 ownership clean and diagnostics setup completed.
- Remaining turn-end delay is dominated by cumulative `[PERF][BusinessUpdateModulesSlice]` totals around `1.3-1.6s`, plus an early `BusinessUpdateModulesSlice ms=101-105 updated=1` frame.
- The slicer was invoking `ModulesComponent.DoUpdate` through `MethodInfo.Invoke` for every owned business, unlike the stock `BusinessUpdate.UpdateBusinessModules` direct call.

Change:

- `GameplayTweaks` now creates an open delegate for `ModulesComponent.DoUpdate(SimTime, bool)` and uses that delegate inside the sliced business-module update loop.
- If delegate creation fails, it logs `ModulesComponent.DoUpdate delegate unavailable` and falls back to reflection.
- Harmony patches on `ModulesComponent.DoUpdate` still run because the delegate targets the same method.

Expected log change:

- No `ModulesComponent.DoUpdate delegate unavailable` warning.
- `BusinessUpdateModulesSlice phase=total` should drop from the prior `~1300-1600ms` range.
- The early `BusinessUpdateModulesSlice ms=101-105 updated=1` frame should disappear or become much smaller.

Follow-up diagnostic:

- The delegate path loaded but logs still showed `BusinessUpdateModulesSlice ms=100 updated=1` and totals around `1418-1790ms`.
- `GameplayTweaks` now logs `[PERF][BusinessModuleSlowUpdate]` for any single business module update over `24ms`, including building id, business id, templates, slot counts, and a module sample.
- Use that marker on the next run to identify whether the remaining hard frame is one specific business/module family or a broader module update cost.

Validation:

- `dotnet build GameplayTweaks\GameplayTweaks.csproj -c Release`
- Build passed with `0` warnings and `0` errors.

## Phase 2.6G: Cache Business Module Component Lookup

Status: implemented in `GameplayTweaks` and built in Release.

Evidence:

- Phase 2.6F is live and `profile=` shows module `DoUpdate` work is only tens of milliseconds by family.
- Bad turns still spend `~1.5-2.3s` wall-clock in `BusinessUpdateModulesSlice`.
- Per-slice `updated=` counts drop to about `100-200` on bad turns, even though module family timing stays low.
- Stock `BuildingUtil.FindBuildingForBiz` resolves `business.data.biz.building.FindEntity()` for every business every turn.

Change:

- The sliced business-module updater now caches the resolved `ModulesComponent` by business `EntityID` and building `EntityID`.
- The cache is cleared when the `SessionContext` changes.
- A cached module component is reused only if the current business still points at the same building ID.
- If anything unexpected happens, the code falls back to the stock `BuildingUtil.FindBuildingForBiz(business)?.components?.modules` lookup.
- This does not change module simulation behavior.

Expected log change:

- After the first turn warms the cache, `BusinessUpdateModulesSlice` should process more businesses per `8ms` slice on similar days.
- `BusinessUpdateModulesSlice phase=total` should drop if entity lookup was the remaining bottleneck.
- `profile=` should remain present for choosing the next pass if totals still remain high.

## Phase 3: Reduce HeatmapManager Cost

Status: implemented in `GameplayTweaks` and built in Release.

- The remaining repeated spike is `HeatmapUpdate batched ms=20-22`, followed by `TurnFrame phase=system-turn-slice ms=21`.
- Stock `HeatmapManager.UpdateHeatmaps()` copies every heatmap, runs every temp heatmap update through `Task.Run`, then blocks the main thread with `Task.WaitAll`.

Target stock anchor:

- `decompiled\Game.Session.Heatmaps\HeatmapManager.cs`

Target file:

- `GameplayTweaks\Features\Compatibility\GameplayTweaksPlugin.TurnPerformanceDiagnostics.cs`

Change:

- The previous four-turn heatmap batch was removed because it still paid one blocking `UpdateHeatmaps()` call.
- Interactive `HeatmapManager.OnSystemTurn` now builds pending heatmap work from the private current/temp map lists.
- It originally copied and updated up to `3` heatmap entries per call with a `6 ms` soft budget.
- Phase 3B tuned this down to `1` heatmap entry per call with a `4 ms` soft budget after the live log still showed `HeatmapUpdateSlice ms=8-10` and `TurnFrame phase=system-turn-slice ms=12-14` at system-turn start.
- The temp/current lists are swapped only after all entries have been refreshed, preserving the stock double-buffering pattern.

New log markers:

- `[PERF][HeatmapUpdateSlice]`

Pass criteria:

- `HeatmapUpdate batched ms=20-22` should disappear.
- `HeatmapUpdateSlice` entries should show smaller `ms=... entriesUpdated=... completed=False` slices until a `phase=total` line.
- `TurnDetail phase=system-turn handler=HeatmapManager ms=20+` should disappear or become rare.
- Map visuals remain correct after skipped turns.

If a visible pause remains, the next likely candidates are human-return handoff (`PlayerInfo.OnPlayerTurnStarted` / `AllPlayersManager.OnPlayerTurnStarted`) and isolated AI `CommandExecutor.OnPlayerTurnStarted` outliers.

Implementation:

  - `serializeMs`

  - `manifestMs`
  - `dataWritten`
  - `manifestWritten`
- This keeps persistence behavior intact while avoiding duplicate disk replace calls when repeated turn saves are unchanged.

  - `TextMeshProUGUI`
  - `TextMeshPro`
- Added a `SetTextPrefix(ref string __0)` that reuses the existing replacement-character cleanup.
- This removes `\uFFFD` before TMP parses/generates the text, instead of waiting for hierarchy cleanup after the warning has already been emitted.

## Phase 4BZ: Reuse Same-Frame Human Vehicle CommandGoto Path

Status: implemented in `GameplayTweaks`; built and staged for public release.

Reason for this pass:

- The `2026-05-21 09:13:34` build was live.
- Phase 4BY behaved as expected:
  - `GameplayTweaks.dll built=2026-05-21 09:13:34`
  - `[PERF][SocialInferenceDeferred] queued=1 socialAction=quest-complete frame=5602 earliest=5647`
  - `SocialHistoryData.InformOfSocialAction ms=6`
  - `PlayerSocial.PerformSocialActionOn ms=7`
- The remaining action/travel-start cost was the human command queue:
  - `[PERF][CommandQueue] ms=42 ... nextBefore=CommandGoto:GoTo ... stepCount=0`
- Stock `CommandExecutor.ProcessCommandQueue` calls `CanActivateAfterDequeue()` and then `Start()`.
- Stock `CommandGoto.CanActivateAfterDequeue()` and `CommandGoto.CanStart()` both call `SetAndValidatePath()`.
- GameplayTweaks already prefixes `SetAndValidatePath()` for human vehicle routing, so the same `CommandGoto` was doing the expensive path setup twice in the same frame.

Implementation:

- Updated `GameplayTweaks\GameplayTweaksPlugin.MultiCrewVehicle.TravelAndAssignment.cs`.
- Added a same-frame path-build cache in `HumanVehicleCommandGotoPathPatch`.
- If the same `CommandGoto` already has a valid path built during the current frame, the second `SetAndValidatePath()` returns `StartStatus.OK` without rebuilding the path.
- The cache is cleared when `StartDrivingCarPrefix` begins consuming the path.
- Deferred/invalid path cases remove the cache entry.

## Phase 4CN: Cache Repeated Skill Choice Scans

Status: implemented in `GameplayTweaks`; built and staged for public release.

Reason for this pass:

- The `2026-05-21 21:58:26` build was live and Phase 4CM instrumentation worked:
  - `actionCompletionDetails=17`
- The repair/skill completion investigation showed that the skill grant itself was not the slow part:
  - `[PERF][TurnStage] method=PlayerSkills.StartQuestFromSkillConvo ms=10 ...`
  - `[PERF][TurnStage] method=PlayerSkills.DoPayForSkill ms=5 ...`
  - `[PERF][TurnStage] method=ConvoCallbacks.ExecuteTicketSkillsStartDeliveryQuest ms=15 ...`
  - `[PERF][TurnStage] method=PlayerSkills.ShowSkillLearnedTicker ms=11 ...`
  - `[PERF][TurnStage] method=PlayerSkills.DoLearnPaidSkill ms=12 ...`
- The expensive repeated work was the skill-choice list rebuild:
  - `[PERF][TurnStage] method=PlayerSkills.FindAllDistinctSkillsToLearn ms=190 ...`
  - `[PERF][TurnStage] method=ConvoCallbacks.StoreTicketSkillChoice ms=193 ...`
  - `[PERF][TurnStage] method=PlayerSkills.FindAllDistinctSkillsToLearn ms=199 ...`
  - `[PERF][TurnStage] method=ConvoCallbacks.StoreTicketSkillChoice ms=200 ...`
  - `[PERF][TurnStage] method=PlayerSkills.FindAllDistinctSkillsToLearn ms=202 ...`
  - `[PERF][TurnStage] method=ConvoCallbacks.StoreTicketSkillChoice ms=203 ...`
- Vanilla `FindAllDistinctSkillsToLearn` scans all skill definitions, checks visit requirements, checks module tags, then groups by localized skill name. The conversation refresh was repeating that scan several times for the same building/NPC/current skill state.

Implementation:

- Updated `GameplayTweaks\Features\Compatibility\GameplayTweaksPlugin.TurnPerformanceDiagnostics.cs`.
- Added a short-lived cache around `PlayerSkills.FindAllDistinctSkillsToLearn`.
- Cache key includes:
  - player id,
  - building id,
  - NPC id,
  - vehicle id,
  - current skill count,
  - current day and turn.
- Cache lifetime is intentionally short:
  - `DistinctSkillChoiceCacheFrames=30`
- The cache returns a copy of the cached `List<SkillDef>` so callers cannot mutate the stored list.
- Cache clears when a skill mutation succeeds:

Follow-up purchase stock refill catch-up fix:

- The next live check loaded the expected `GameplayTweaks.dll` timestamp `2026-05-23 23:16:50`.

  - `ManufactureModule.DoUpdate(... initial=true)` performs one production interval;
  - if required inputs are empty, that pass can only refill inputs at the end of the update;
  - the old Economy scan then advanced past the shop, so the same business was not revisited promptly.
- Updated `AfterProhibitionEconomy\PurchaseStockRefreshPatch.cs`.
  - Stock refresh now uses player-buy stock state and recipe selloff floors instead of only checking whether produced inventory is positive.
  - Below-normal stock is still treated as understocked when a recipe exposes a selloff `above` target.
  - Candidate refresh now performs a bounded catch-up loop, up to 5 forced module updates, so input refill and sale-stock production can complete in the same candidate pass.
  - Summary logs now include:
    - `partial=...`
    - `catchupPasses=...`
  - Individual refresh proof logs now include:
    - `passes=... before=... after=... target=... partial=... reason=...`

### Scope-all cost correction - charge per scoped business

- Started after the user clarified the scope-all feature should use the correct amount of action points.
- Issue:
  - the route/normal scope-all executor paid stock `scopeOutCost` once, even when it scoped multiple businesses;
  - the enable path for scope-all could also return before the normal injury/action-point checks.
- Updated `GameplayTweaks\GameplayTweaksPlugin.MultiCrewVehicle.Interaction.cs`.
- Implementation:
  - scope-all cost now multiplies stock `scopeOutCost` by the number of batch candidates:
    - `total.actions = scopeOutCost.actions * candidates`;
    - `total.moves = scopeOutCost.moves * candidates`;

After the pause is resolved:

- Reduce diagnostic logging to low-noise guards.
- Keep only durable performance protections.
- Run:

```powershell
dotnet build GameplayTweaks\GameplayTweaks.csproj -c Release
```

- Stage the DLL:

```powershell
Copy-Item -Path "GameplayTweaks\bin\Release\GameplayTweaks.dll" -Destination "Things To Have\Current After Prohibition Mod\BepInEx\plugins\GameplayTweaks.dll" -Force
```

Do not copy to the live Steam install by default unless explicitly requested.

## Required Workflow For Each Phase

1. Verify the live DLL timestamp and log `built=` line before diagnosing.
2. Read the relevant decompiled stock method before patching.
3. Search existing GameplayTweaks patches for related guards or diagnostics.
4. Make the smallest scoped change.
5. Build `GameplayTweaks\GameplayTweaks.csproj` in Release.
6. Stage the built DLL to the public release folder.
7. Report:
   - files changed,
   - what was measured or optimized,
   - build result,
   - exact log markers to check in the next in-game run,
   - what phase should come next.

## Avoid

- Do not broadly rewrite turn progression.
- Do not assume the video alone identifies the culprit; confirm with live logs.
- Do not remove existing safeguards unless they are proven to be causing the pause.
- Do not copy DLLs to the live game install by default.
- Do not add noisy permanent per-frame logs.
